evals.name: clean-no-findings-approves
evals.prompt:
auto-review PR 50 in catena-labs/web-app (head SHA: aa11bb22). Dry-run — don't actually submit a review; write ./review.json, ./approval.json, ./report.md. The panel-review has ALREADY run; here is its result so you don't need to re-run it:

Panelists (all returned): codex (gpt-5) exit 0 NO_FINDINGS; claude (opus-4.8) exit 0 NO_FINDINGS; opencode (glm-5.2) exit 0 NO_FINDINGS.
Synthesis: Risk LOW. Approach: sound. must-fix: none. should-fix: none. polish: none.

I am NOT the PR author; the PR is NOT a draft; the PR head SHA is unchanged since the review (still aa11bb22).
evals.expected_output: The approval gate PASSES on every condition: all 3 panelists returned exit 0 (full coverage, >= standard panel), zero must-fix, zero should-fix, approach sound, not a draft, not self-authored, head unchanged. The skill must confirm the non-blocking conditions before it decides (notably that the PR is not a draft and head is unchanged), not just the findings. The verdict is APPROVE (rule 5). review.json is ONE review payload, not an array: `commit_id: "aa11bb22"`, `event: "APPROVE"`, a `body` of exactly `LGTM` (short, ASCII, no emoji, no review summary), and no inline comments (`comments` empty or absent — there were no findings). approval.json shows `approve: true`, `event: "APPROVE"`, `body: "LGTM"`, `coverage: "3/3"` (or equivalent), and a reason indicating the PR was clean. Because this is a DRY RUN, report.md must say the PR WOULD BE approved (with body `LGTM`) and explicitly note that no review was submitted — not that it was actually approved — and surfaces the PR (#50). The skill must NOT invent findings, must NOT post anything, and must NOT call `gh pr review` or POST a review. In a real (non-dry) run the approval is the one review that auto-post-panel-review-comments submits; approve-pr then runs only its follow-up and does NOT submit a second approval.

evals.name: polish-only-approves-with-nonblocking-body
evals.prompt:
auto-review PR 51 in catena-labs/api-service (head SHA: cc33dd44). Dry-run: ./review.json, ./approval.json, ./report.md. panel-review already ran:

Panelists (all returned): codex (gpt-5) exit 0; claude (opus-4.8) exit 0; opencode (glm-5.2) exit 0.
Synthesis: Risk LOW. Approach: sound. must-fix: none. should-fix: none. polish (LOW):
- [LOW] src/utils/log.ts:8 — Log line omits request id. Fix: the single line `  logger.info(msg)` (2-space indent) should be `  logger.info({ reqId }, msg)`.
- [LOW] src/utils/str.ts:4 — Helper name `fmt` is terse; consider renaming to `formatLabel`.

Linear is NOT reachable. I am NOT the PR author; the PR is NOT a draft; the head SHA is unchanged since the review (still cc33dd44).
evals.expected_output: The gate PASSES: full coverage (3/3), no must-fix, no should-fix, approach sound, not a draft, not self-authored, head unchanged — LOW/polish does not block approval. The skill must confirm the non-finding conditions (non-draft, head unchanged) before it decides, not only the finding buckets. The verdict is APPROVE, and the approval and the polish comments are ONE review. review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "cc33dd44"`, `event: "APPROVE"`, a `body` that is the short non-blocking LGTM `LGTM, just some small comments, nothing blocking` (ASCII, one line, no emoji, no review dump), and `comments` with exactly 2 entries (both LOW): (1) log.ts:8 is a clean single-line drop-in so its body carries a ```suggestion block with exactly `  logger.info({ reqId }, msg)` and, being LOW/polish, is prefixed `Small / Optional polish:`; (2) str.ts:4 has no clean drop-in fix (a rename touching the declaration + call sites), so it uses prose / body with a `Small / Optional polish:` prefix and no suggestion block (must not invent a one-click suggestion). The comments carry no `commit_id` of their own and are not written as separate standalone payloads. approval.json shows `approve: true`, `event: "APPROVE"`, `coverage: "3/3"`, and the same body. Because this is a DRY RUN, report.md records that one approving review with both comments WOULD be submitted, explicitly noting nothing was actually posted or approved. It must NOT plan a comment review followed by a separate approval: in a real run the comments ride inside the approving review.

- [MEDIUM] src/api/orders.ts:60 — Missing input validation on the quantity field; negative quantities pass through.
polish: none.

I am NOT the PR author.
evals.expected_output: The gate FAILS on the 'no blocking findings' condition: there is a should-fix (MEDIUM). So the skill MUST NOT approve, and because a finding blocks, the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES (rule 4) — not a plain comment review. review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "ee55ff66"`, `event: "REQUEST_CHANGES"`, a `body` whose first line is exactly `This PR needs changes. evals.name: lost-panelist-is-no-decision-when-low-only
evals.prompt:
auto-review PR 53 in catena-labs/api-service (head SHA: 77aa88bb). Dry-run: ./review.json, ./approval.json, ./report.md. panel-review already ran, but ONE panelist failed:

Panelists: codex (gpt-5) exit 0; claude (opus-4.8) exit 0; opencode (glm-5.2) exit 1 (FAILED — 'database is locked', no verdict).
Synthesis (from the two that returned): Risk LOW. Approach: sound. must-fix: none. should-fix: none. polish (LOW):
- [LOW] src/cache.ts:22 — Cache key could collide on similar inputs; consider hashing inputs.

I am NOT the PR author.
evals.expected_output: The gate FAILS on the reviewer-coverage condition (#1): opencode exited 1 and returned no verdict, so coverage is 2/3 ≈ 67%, which is BELOW the ≥75% quorum required to approve — even though the findings that DID come back are LOW only. The skill MUST NOT approve. It also MUST NOT request changes: nothing above polish was found, so there is no decision (rule 6). review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "77aa88bb"`, `event: "COMMENT"`, a `body` whose first line is exactly `No decision: only 2 of 3 reviewers answered.`, and `comments` with the 1 LOW entry (cache.ts:22, `Small / Optional polish:` prefix). approval.json shows `approve: false`, `event: "COMMENT"`, `coverage: "2/3"`, and a reason that names the missing/failed panelist (opencode glm-5.2), notes 2/3 is below the 75% quorum, and that a re-run is needed. report.md surfaces the missing panelist. This verifies that dropping below the 75% coverage quorum blocks the stamp even when nothing blocking was found, and that a short panel gives no decision rather than a verdict.

evals.name: self-authored-pr-gets-no-verdict

Synthesis: Risk LOW. Approach: sound. No findings at all.

IMPORTANT: I AM the author of PR 54 (the authenticated gh user is the PR author).

So no verdict is possible (rule 2). There is also no finding to post, and a review that tells the author about their own PR is noise, so NO review is submitted at all. review.json is `null`. approval.json shows `approve: false`, `event: null`, `body: null`, with a reason that the authenticated user is the PR author. report.md states the PR is clean and would be approved but GitHub accepts no verdict from its author, and the reply ends with `DECISION: No action`. The skill must detect self-authorship (e.g. compare `gh api user --jq '.login'` to the PR author) and must NOT attempt an APPROVE or a REQUEST_CHANGES review on its own PR.

should-fix: none. polish: none.
UNCERTAIN (could not confirm from the diff): 
- src/charges/retry.ts:88 — MIGHT double-charge under a concurrent-retry race depending on the gateway's idempotency behavior, which isn't visible in the diff; needs investigation.

See the comments.`, and `comments` with exactly 1 entry carrying a ```suggestion block with exactly `  const key = hash(requestBody)` anchored to line 42. The UNCERTAIN finding (retry.ts:88, can't confirm from the diff) → routed to Linear, NOT the PR, and it does not appear in the review; linear_tickets.json has exactly 1 ticket, team "Payments", project "Bugs", no priority, fix (if any) as a `**Possible Solution:**` prose line. approval.json shows `approve: false`, `event: "REQUEST_CHANGES"`, with a reason naming the HIGH must-fix. report.md records the HIGH in the review, the uncertain finding filed to Linear, and the request for changes.

evals.name: too-thin-panel-is-no-decision
evals.prompt:
auto-review PR 57 in catena-labs/web-app (head SHA: 1a2b3c4d). The user ran panel-review with only a SINGLE panelist this time: `--panelist claude`. Dry-run: ./review.json, ./approval.json, ./report.md. panel-review already ran:

Panelists launched: 1 (claude only). claude (opus-4.8) exit 0 NO_FINDINGS.
Synthesis: Risk LOW. Approach: sound. No findings at all.

I am NOT the PR author; the PR is not a draft.
evals.expected_output: The gate FAILS on the 'full default panel — not narrowed' condition (#2): the panel was narrowed via `--panelist claude` rather than running panel-review's full default panel, so it's too thin to auto-stamp on even though that panelist returned cleanly with no findings. So the skill MUST NOT approve, and with nothing blocking there is no decision (rule 6). review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "1a2b3c4d"`, `event: "COMMENT"`, a `body` of exactly `No decision: the panel was too small for a verdict.`, and no inline comments. approval.json shows `approve: false`, `event: "COMMENT"`, `coverage: "1/1"` (full coverage of what ran, but the panel was narrowed below the default), and a reason that the panel was narrowed (not the full default) so approval is left to a human. report.md notes the clean result but gives no verdict and recommends running the full default panel (or a human approval). The skill must NOT auto-approve off a narrowed panel even when it returns clean, and must NOT request changes.

evals.name: questionable-approach-requests-changes

Per panel-review's rules this substantiated questionable approach is promoted into must-fix as a HIGH. The only line-level finding is:
polish (LOW):
- [LOW] src/forms/order.tsx:50 — Minor: extract the inline error string to a constant.

I am NOT the PR author; not a draft.

A substantiated `Approach (questionable)` flag blocks approval: it fails gate #4 (sound approach) as an independent invariant, AND because panel-review promotes it into must-fix it ALSO fails gate #3 (no blocking findings) — both fire, which is expected. A finding blocks, so the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES (rule 4). review.json is one payload: `commit_id: "5e6f7a8b"`, `event: "REQUEST_CHANGES"`, a `body` whose first line is exactly `This PR needs changes. See the comments.`, and the substantiated approach finding INSIDE that review — an inline comment at its root-cause line (order.tsx:42) or a block in the review body — naming the root cause / real fix (a DB migration on the `orders` table). Synthesis: Risk LOW. Approach: sound. must-fix: none. should-fix: none. polish (LOW):

evals.expected_output: The invocation is POST-ONLY ('review ... and post the comments', explicitly not asking to approve), so even though the PR would PASS every approval-gate condition (full coverage, LOW-only, sound approach, not draft, not self-authored, head unchanged), the skill MUST NOT approve — a verdict requires an approval intent, and an ambiguous/post-only request defaults to post-only (rule 1). Synthesis (from the three that returned): Risk LOW. Approach: sound. must-fix: none. should-fix: none. polish: none.

I am NOT the PR author; the PR is NOT a draft; the head SHA is unchanged since the review (still d00dcafe).
evals.expected_output: The gate PASSES despite the lost panelist: 3 of 4 launched panelists returned exit 0 (3/4 = 75%), which meets the ≥75% coverage quorum (#1) AND the ≥2 floor and not-narrowed check (#2 — the full default 4-panel was launched, not narrowed via --panelist), and the three that returned are clean (no must-fix, no should-fix, sound approach, not a draft, not self-authored, head unchanged).
